title: Full of grace to people, thanked by few.
subtitle: Why the punishment has not come yet
then: Right after the deniers asked when the punishment would come, Allah says He is full of grace to mankind. Ibn Kathir explains {reward}He abundantly bestows His blessings on them even though they wrong themselves{/reward}, and still {trap}they do not give thanks, except a few.{/trap}
now: You skipped Fajr again, snapped at your mother, and still woke up healthy, with coffee and a paycheck coming. {reward}The blessings did not stop.{/reward} That is not proof nothing matters. It is grace giving you room.
old: If nothing bad happens when I mess up, it must not matter.
new: The good that keeps coming despite my faults is grace, and it deserves thanks.
try: Write down three blessings you received today despite something you did wrong.

title: He knows what your chest hides and what you say.
subtitle: No gap between the hidden and the shown
then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}He knows what is hidden in their hearts just as He knows what is easily visible.{/idea} He cites verses saying it is the same to Him whether speech is hidden or open, and that He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
now: You smile in the meeting while resenting your manager. You post the Ramadan quote while holding a grudge. {idea}He sees the chest and the caption.{/idea} You can stop working so hard on two versions of yourself.
old: What I feel inside is my business, as long as I act fine.
new: Allah sees my inner state as clearly as my actions, so I can work on both honestly.
try: Pick one feeling you hide behind a smile. Tell Allah about it in your own words.

title: Nothing hidden anywhere is missing from the Record.
subtitle: All of it written in a clear Book
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}there is nothing in the heaven and the earth but it is in a Clear Book.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse saying Allah knows all that is in the heavens and earth, it is all in the Book, and that is easy for Him.
now: The sadaqah you gave years ago that you forgot about. The tears no one saw. The small cruelty you hoped would fade. {idea}None of it fell through the cracks.{/idea} That is comfort and caution together.
old: Small things I did long ago are gone and forgotten.
new: Every hidden thing is written, so no good I do is wasted and no wrong is lost.
try: Do one small good deed today knowing it will be written, even if you forget it.

title: The Quran settles what people argued over.
subtitle: A moderate word of truth
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran narrates the truth about matters the Children of Israel differed on, {idea}such as their different opinions about Isa.{/idea} It came with {idea}the moderate word of truth and justice{/idea}: that he was a servant of Allah and one of His noble Prophets.
now: The family argument about an uncle who either did everything wrong or could do no wrong. The online fight where every side is extreme. {idea}Truth is often the just middle.{/idea} You can look for it instead of picking a camp.
old: In any argument, I have to pick the side that sounds strongest.
new: The truth is often balanced, and I can look for the just word between extremes.
try: In one disagreement today, say something fair about both sides before giving your view.

title: For the believers, a guide and a mercy.
subtitle: What the Quran does in a heart
then: After settling old disagreements, the verse says the Quran is {idea}guidance for the hearts of those who believe in it{/idea}, and {reward}a mercy to them.{/reward} The surah opened the same way: guidance and good news for the believers.
now: It is a heavy night. You open the Quran not to study, just because nothing else helps. {reward}One verse lands exactly where it hurts.{/reward} That is the mercy part.
old: The Quran is mostly a list of rules.
new: The Quran is guidance and a mercy, something my heart can lean on.
try: Tonight, read a few verses slowly when you feel low, just for comfort.

title: Your Lord will judge between them.
subtitle: Some arguments are settled on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah will decide between them {idea}on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. He is All-Mighty and {idea}All-Knowing, knowing all that His servants do and say.{/idea}
now: The inheritance dispute that never resolved. The friend who still tells the story wrong. {idea}Not every argument needs to be won this week.{/idea} Some you can leave with the One who knows everything.
old: If I do not win this argument now, injustice wins.
new: Allah will judge every dispute fairly, so I do not have to settle all of them myself.
try: Choose one old argument and let it go to Allah, out loud, today.

title: Rely on Allah. You are on clear truth.
subtitle: Steadiness when opposed
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to {idea}put his trust in Allah in all his affairs and convey the Message{/idea}, because he was following manifest truth, even though opposed by those who opposed him.
now: You are the only one in the family keeping halal income, or the one who will not cut corners at work. People push back. {reward}Being opposed does not make you wrong.{/reward} Lean on Allah and keep going.
old: When many people push back, I should probably give in.
new: If I am on the truth, I can rely on Allah and stay steady.
try: Say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil before facing someone who opposes what is right.

title: You cannot make someone hear who turns away.
subtitle: The limits of a messenger
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Prophet ﷺ {trap}cannot cause them to hear anything that will benefit them{/trap}, like those whose hearts are veiled and whose ears are deaf. The verse pictures people {trap}turning their backs and fleeing{/trap} from the call.
now: You have explained it to your friend five different ways. You sent the article, the lecture, the gentle text. {idea}Some people are walking away while you talk.{/idea} That is not your failure.
old: If someone does not listen, I have not explained it well enough.
new: My job is to speak well; making someone hear belongs to Allah.
try: Stop pushing one conversation that is not landing. Make dua for that person instead.

title: Only those who believe will truly listen.
subtitle: Who the message reaches
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}those who have hearing and insight will respond{/reward}: those whose hearing and sight benefit their hearts, and who are {idea}humble towards Allah and the Message.{/idea}
now: You have heard the same khutbah topic ten times. One Friday, it suddenly hits. {idea}What changed was not the words. It was your heart.{/idea} Hearing well begins with being humble.
old: I have heard this before, so I already know it.
new: Real hearing comes from a humble heart, not from having heard it before.
try: At the next reminder you hear, ask Allah first to open your heart to it.

title: A creature from the earth will speak.
subtitle: A sign near the end of time
then: Ibn Kathir says this beast will emerge at the end of time, {trap}when mankind has become corrupt and neglected the commands of Allah.{/trap} He cites the hadith in Muslim: {idea}hasten to do good deeds before six things appear{/idea}, including the beast.
now: You follow end-times videos online with real interest. But the Prophet ﷺ pointed the signs back at deeds. {idea}The question is not when it comes, but what you do now.{/idea}
old: Signs of the end are interesting things to know about.
new: Every sign of the end is a call to hurry toward good deeds today.
try: Do one good deed today that you have been putting off.
